title: Requested accelerator and actual runtime resources are separate facts
summary: A selector such as --gpu T4 is an allocation request, not sufficient evidence of the device or its usable memory. The worker must inspect the actual GPU identity, CUDA-visible memory, host MemTotal/MemAvailable and disk before model loading. In the qualified Gemma run, the T4 exposed 14,912 MiB CUDA memory and the host exposed 12,975 MiB total RAM; literal 15,000 MiB gates were therefore wrong even though the correct T4 had been allocated.
evidence_note: Live T4 evidence: Tesla T4, 14,912 MiB CUDA-visible GPU memory, 12,975 MiB host memory, with successful later NF4/LoRA work after calibrated gates. Current upstream also warns that accelerator availability is entitlement/capacity dependent and status should be used to inspect actual hardware.
invariants: Keep nominal accelerator identity distinct from observed GPU memory.
Worker sanity thresholds use realistic exposed-resource floors, not marketing/nominal numbers.
Check MemAvailable as well as MemTotal before memory-heavy work.
Resource mismatch fails before downloading/loading the expensive model when practical.
